excerpts.text: **SPHEREx** (**Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer**)[[4]](#cite_note-4) is a [near-infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared_astronomy "Infrared astronomy") [space observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_observatory "Space observatory") that is performing an [all-sky survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-sky_survey "All-sky survey") to measure the [near-infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near-infrared "Near-infrared") spectra of approximately 450 million [galaxies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy "Galaxy"). In February 2019, SPHEREx was selected by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") for its next [Medium-Class Explorers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explorers_program#Medium-Class_Explorers_(MIDEX) "Explorers program") mission, beating out two competing mission concepts: *[Arcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcus_(satellite) "Arcus (satellite)")* and [FINESSE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Infrared_Exoplanet_Spectroscopy_Survey_Explorer "Fast Infrared Exoplanet Spectroscopy Survey Explorer").[[5]](#cite_note-nasa20190213-5)[[6]](#cite_note-Proposals_2017-6) SPHEREx launched on 11 March 2025 on a [Falcon 9 Block 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falcon_9_Block_5 "Falcon 9 Block 5") rocket alongside the [PUNCH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarimeter_to_Unify_the_Corona_and_Heliosphere "Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere") microsatellites from [Vandenberg Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vandenberg_Space_Force_Base "Vandenberg Space Force Base").[[2]](#cite_note-launch-date-2)[[3]](#cite_note-scrubs-3) The principal investigator is James Bock at [California Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Institute_of_Technology "California Institute of Technology") (Caltech) in [Pasadena, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California").

SPHEREx was selected as the winner in February 2019, and the mission was approved to proceed with detailed planning.[[5]](#cite_note-nasa20190213-5) On 4 February 2021, NASA announced they had selected the [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX") [Falcon 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falcon_9 "Falcon 9") to launch the spacecraft, and total cost of the launch would be US$98.8 million.[[18]](#cite_note-nasa4feb21-18) In August 2022 NASA announced that the 4 microsatellites of the [PUNCH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarimeter_to_Unify_the_Corona_and_Heliosphere "Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere") constellation would be launched as rideshare payloads together with SPHEREx.[[19]](#cite_note-nasa-20220803-19) The mission launched on 11 March 2025.[[2]](#cite_note-launch-date-2) [First light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_light_(astronomy) "First light (astronomy)") was in April 2025.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Regular science operation started on 1 May 2025.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

excerpts.text: SPHEREx was successfully launched on March 11, 2025.

SPHEREx was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at the Vandenberg Space Force Base, California on March 11, 2025. The launch was procured by NASA's Launch Services Program and was conducted as a shared mission with the Polarimeter to UNify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) spacecraft.

* March 11, 2025: SPHEREx was successfully launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California at 8.10 p.m. PDT. Ground controllers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California established communications with the space observatory at 9:31 p.m PDT. 11)
